newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Reserve Bank supports rand - dealers.
newsitem.headline: S.African Reserve Bank supports rand - dealers.

text.p: The Reserve Bank stepped in to defend the rand in Tuesday afternoon trade as it weakened more than six cents from its best intraday level, dealers said.

The rand weakened from a day's best level of 4.3790 bid against the dollar to 4.4530 by 1204 GMT after central bank governor Chris Stals said that the rand's recent strength could be a slight over-adjustment.
Dealers said that the central bank had sold dollars into the currency market from the 4.41 level upwards.
"The big banks were given orders to sell dollars," one trader said.
Another trader at one of the country's big four banks said: "Yes, it (the central bank) has been selling dollars from all sorts of levels...from 4.41 upwards."
Reserve Bank officials were not immediately available for comment.
By 1320 GMT, the rand had regained some composure to trade at 4.4270/4300 against the dollar from 4.4075/4105 overnight.
